Regression: pre-existing test_volume_discounts.py TestPaperGradient (paper 8-row gradient), TestRBACWithDiscount (client/reseller retail/wholesale strip), and all other-module discount checks still pass when the DTF map key is empty. State was fully restored: volume_discounts_by_module={default:[8 default tiers], dtf:[]} — dtf empty means fallback to default per spec.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now uses TWO module-level globals for volume discounts (_VOLUME_DISCOUNTS_MAP + _CURRENT_MODULE). The _CURRENT_MODULE global is set by set_calc_module() as the first line of every /api/calc/* handler and read inside scrub(). This is safe under a single asyncio event loop, but any two concurrent /api/calc/* requests could interleave set_calc_module→scrub across await points, causing tier bleed between modules. Recommend threading the module name explicitly through scrub(data, role, module=...) instead of a global. This is the same class of issue flagged in iteration 30, now amplified.

Settings Pydantic model retains BOTH legacy `volume_discounts` (list) and new `volume_discounts_by_module` (dict). PUT accepts either but scrub() only consults the map. If a caller PUTs only the legacy field (e.g. old client), the map is preserved but they may believe they updated tiers — silent divergence. Consider deprecating the legacy field or auto-syncing legacy→map['default'] on PUT.

MODULES_VD in Settings.js uses keys ('default','paper','booklet','large-format','stickers','dtf','embroidery','laser','direct-print','channel-letters','sublimation','roll-stickers') that must exactly match set_calc_module() strings in server.py. Any typo (e.g. renaming 'direct-print' to 'directprint') would silently make custom tiers a no-op. Consider a single shared constant or a backend-provided enum.
server.py still exceeds 3200 lines — modularization strongly recommended (repeated from iteration 30).
GET /api/materials still ignores ?category=<x> query param (repeated from iteration 30).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Per-module VD tests live in /app/backend/tests/test_volume_discounts_per_module.py. Because this file mutates settings.volume_discounts_by_module (a global doc) via a module-scoped fixture, it MUST be run in a single xdist group — pytestmark = pytest.mark.xdist_group('volume_discount_settings') is already set to serialize with the older test_volume_discounts.py which shares the same group. If you run both files in parallel workers WITHOUT xdist grouping you will see false-positive failures at TestOtherModules::test_dtf_qty_500_discount because DTF custom tiers can leak. Frontend testids: vd-module-select (12 options), vd-add, vd-row, vd-qty, vd-pct, vd-remove, vd-copy-default (only shown for non-default modules). Save via save-settings-button. Module keys used by set_calc_module in backend (must match MODULES_VD frontend list exactly): paper, booklet, large-format, stickers, dtf, embroidery, laser, direct-print, channel-letters, sublimation, roll-stickers. Sublimation calc test still skipped (needs sublimation-eligible product seeded) — non-blocking.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature works as specified. Only observation: during test file authoring I encountered an xdist worker-race in fixture teardown (two workers each captured their own 'original_map', last-writer-wins on restore, leaving DTF custom tiers in DB and cascading a false-positive failure in the legacy test_volume_discounts.py::TestOtherModules::test_dtf_qty_500_discount which assumes default tiers). Mitigation: added pytestmark = pytest.mark.xdist_group('volume_discount_settings') to the new file so it serializes with the pre-existing file. Verified by running the file with a single worker (-o addopts=): all 13 pass cleanly, and final DB state is the requested clean state {default:[8 defaults], dtf:[]}.
